title: [Bug]: Nextcloud 31 LDAP Configuration Not Working On Nextcloud 32
body:
### ⚠️ This issue respects the following points: ⚠️

- [x] This is a **bug**, not a question or a configuration/webserver/proxy issue.
- [x] This issue is **not** already reported on [Github](https://github.com/nextcloud/server/issues?q=is%3Aopen+is%3Aissue+label%3Abug) OR [Nextcloud Community Forum](https://<redacted-host>/) _(I've searched it)_.
- [x] Nextcloud Server **is** up to date. See [Maintenance and Release Schedule](https://github.com/nextcloud/server/wiki/Maintenance-and-Release-Schedule) for supported versions.
- [x] I agree to follow Nextcloud's [Code of Conduct](https://nextcloud.com/contribute/code-of-conduct/).

### Bug description

I have been cloning working Nextcloud 31 servers to version 32.  The upgrade process mostly is going cleanly.  However after upgrade LDAP throws errors about losing connection to ldap.  Randomly pages will not load and report a ldap issue, and then after hitting reload of the page a few times it will finally work.  However, if you reboot the server, LDAP is completely disabled and you cannot log in anymore.  I then disable ldap on the command line and log in with the admin account, which continues to work.  If I change LDAP from tcp/636 to tcp/389 it immediately works.  My current theory is that the setting [x] Turn off SSL certificate validation     might be root cause.  We use this setting for our connections to LDAP.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Upgrade working Nextcloud 31 server to 32 with LDAP configured to turn off ssl certificate validation
2. Immediately you see warnings in the logs and UI failures related to losing ldap connection
3.


### Expected behavior

LDAP should work :)

### Nextcloud Server version

32

### Operating system

RHEL/CentOS

### PHP engine version

PHP 8.3

### Web server

Apache (supported)

### Database engine version

MariaDB

None

comments.author: participant6
comments.body:
@participant4 your issue is the `ldapTLS` setting, which actually refers to enable _StartTLS_. This will not work in combination with plain TLS via (7)636.

Switch the port again to to 7636 (if not already) and run the following to disable it:
`php occ ldap:set-config s01 ldapTLS 0`

Please retry again.

This really would be unrelated to the original report though.

comments.author: participant8
comments.body:
This is not fixed yet. I did an upgrade from 31.0.10 to 32.0.1. And the LDAP connection was lost.
I recovered by setting "ldap server require strong auth = No" in /etc/samba/smb.conf (and restarting samba-ad-dc), and 
```
php occ ldap:set-config s01 ldapHost ldap://localhost
php occ ldap:set-config s01 ldapPort 389

```
(ldapTls was already 0)

After getting into the web admin I noticed thet in the advanced section  turnOffCertCheck was unchecked.

Then I tried to set backup/replica LDAP to ldaps://localhost:636 and checked "disable SSL cert verification" and "disable main server" and clicked "try" and it seems to work.

I did not notice that there is (probably new) config option turnOffCertCheck.
Maybe the turnOffCertCheck should be set to 1 on upgrades, or according to /etc/ldap/ldap.conf or something like that.

>  turnOffCertCheck was unchecked after upgrade. I guess this is a new option, and unchecked by default, right?

No, it is there for a very long time. 

Thanks for the excerpt. Do you also see a line with `Could not turn off SSL certificate validation` in the nextcloud.log?

If not, can you  set the debug level to 0, switch it back to ldaps, and retry? Should not work. But then, does `Turned off SSL certificate validation successfully` appear in the nextcloud.log?

comments.author: participant8

comments.author: participant8
comments.body:
I have switched to LDAPS, and with log_level=0 I see "Turned off SSL certificate validation successfully."
When I enable cert validation, and do a test I get: "Main LDAP not reachable, connecting to backup: Lost connection to LDAP server." That is OK, because main LDAP has self-signed cert, and backup is LDAP without encryption, which is forbidden on the LDAP server (samba).

So now it works as expected, the problem is that it got broken during the upgrade. IMHO the turnOffCertCheck was not defined in version 26 (when I installed this instance), and got explicitly unchecked by upgrading from version 31 -> 32. Before that it honored the content of /etc/ldap/ldap.conf where I have "TLS_REQCERT never". So when upgrading, if turnOffCertCheck is not defined it should be set according to TLS_REQCERT in ldap.conf.

comments.author: participant6
comments.body: `turnOffCertCheck` is older than 12 years: cf. https://github.com/nextcloud/server/blame/9b2e31b6212f8e5f709021557bf525487ed205ab/apps/user_ldap/lib/Configuration.php#L27 It is disabled by default. We have never had an explicit interpretation of `TLS_REQCERT`, this happens in the stack below. And I would expect it continue to work. You can see here what we did before: https://github.com/nextcloud/server/pull/51096/files Also interpreted `turnOffCertCheck`, but only overwrote `LDAPTLS_REQCERT` and it was neither the recommended nor the reliable way to go. If it works for you now, I think the root cause lies elsewhere. Although the stack trace reflects current code, so unlikely that there was old code in opcache. Hard to say.

comments.author: participant9
comments.body:
I also had the problem that my LDAP config no longer worked after updating to NC32 (v31.0.12 → v32.0.3) and it was no longer possible to log in `(Exception":"OC\\ServerNotAvailableException","Message":"Lost connection to LDAP server.)[...]`.
 With `sudo -u www-data php occ ldap:set-config s01 turnOffCertCheck 1` in the nextcloud directory I solved the issue. `ldapTLS` (for reference) is set to 0.
